incidents.name: LaunchZone swapX arbitrary transferFrom
incidents.notes: The swapX implementation behind LaunchZone exposes selector 0x4f1f05bc, which pulls tokens from an arbitrary from-address using the caller's own swap path, so anyone could drain every wallet that had ever approved it.

sources.ref: onchain review: swapX implementation 0x6D8981847Eb3cc2234179d0F0e72F6b6b2421a01 created 2021-10-28T16:43:38Z by 0x6b40b4bef3730c1d484dc0f917a8cd845fe0e85c, unrelated to attack sender 0x7d192fa3a48c307100c3e663050291fff786aa1f; no EIP-1967 Upgraded events on the implementation, age measured from deployment. DeFiHackLabs carries two PoCs for the same flaw (SwapX_exp, ~$1M, and LaunchZone_exp via the 0x0ccee62efec983f3ec4bad3247153009fb483551 proxy, ~$320k); one row is recorded. Loss verified onchain in this transaction: BUSD was pulled from dozens of approver wallets and 230,359.80 BUSD landed in the DND pair.

deployment-basis recheck: the swapX contract's single DELEGATECALL in the attack tx (selector 0x7855da66) goes to 0x6d1879f4151b7f3958b8f5a9cc5e2cc93b95e50d, an address that appears as a PUSH20 constant in the runtime; prestateTracer records zero storage reads on the victim during the tx, so the target is hardcoded rather than looked up, and the runtime is byte-identical at the creation block 12168762 and the incident block 26023089. Deployment is exact; 486.6 days.
